l4_steps.name: Retrieve Final Pax Count & Baggage Weights
l4_steps.input: Check-in closure trigger (T-30 min); APIS/DCS pax manifest
l4_steps.output: Confirmed pax count, checked-bag count, total baggage weight
l4_steps.kpi: Data retrieval completed ≤5 min after check-in close
l4_steps.pain_point: Late pax additions and standby activations in Altéa can shift total bag weights by 200–400 kg after preliminary load plan is locked, requiring full recalculation

l4_steps.name: Calculate Preliminary Weight & Balance
l4_steps.input: Pax manifest, estimated bag weights, fuel uplift from ACARS
l4_steps.output: Preliminary zero fuel weight (ZFW), centre of gravity (CG) estimate, hold allocation plan
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary W&B issued ≤10 min after check-in close
l4_steps.pain_point: Standard passenger weight assumptions (IATA Standard Weights 2023) may under-estimate actual payload on leisure routes with heavy baggage allowances, skewing preliminary CG

l4_steps.name: Validate Dangerous Goods Declarations
l4_steps.input: Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods (SHPD), NOTOC entries from cargo manifest
l4_steps.output: Validated DG NOTOC; approved or rejected DG items with segregation instructions
l4_steps.kpi: DG validation completed ≤15 min before cargo loading commences; zero IATA DGR Part 7 segregation violations
l4_steps.pain_point: Lithium battery shipments (IATA DGR Section II PI 966/967/968) increasingly misclassified by shippers; SITA DGM lacks real-time integration with courier manifest data, requiring manual cross-check

l4_steps.name: Generate Loading Instruction Report (LIR)
l4_steps.input: Approved hold allocation plan, DG segregation instructions, special cargo positions
l4_steps.output: Loading Instruction Report (LIR) specifying bay/pit assignment per item type
l4_steps.kpi: LIR issued to ramp supervisor ≤20 min before scheduled loading start
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper or tablet-based LIR distribution to ramp agents creates version-control risk; last-minute config changes (late cargo acceptance) may not reach all loading teams before loading begins

l4_steps.name: Sort & Route Checked Baggage to Make-Up Area
l4_steps.input: Baggage reconciliation data from Altéa, belt assignment from SITA AMS
l4_steps.output: Sorted baggage staged at correct make-up carousel/area for the flight
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage sortation accuracy ≥99.5%; all bags at make-up area ≥30 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline transfer bags arriving via multiple carriers carry different barcode standards (BCBP vs legacy 10-digit); SITA BagManager reconciliation failures require manual intervention, risking late bags

l4_steps.name: Build ULD / Container per Load Plan Spec
l4_steps.input: LIR bay assignments, sorted baggage at make-up area
l4_steps.output: Loaded ULD/containers tagged with position ID and estimated weight
l4_steps.kpi: ULD build completed per LIR sequence; zero wrong-position items at loading start
l4_steps.pain_point: Wide-body aircraft use mixed ULD types (LD3, LD7, bulk) — incorrect ULD type selection delays loading due to incompatible cargo door dimensions; SITA LoadManager ULD type validation is advisory only

l4_steps.name: Weigh Completed ULD / Container
l4_steps.system: Mettler Toledo ULD Scale + SITA LoadManager
l4_steps.input: Loaded ULD on weigh platform
l4_steps.output: Actual ULD gross weight recorded in LoadManager against plan position
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ULDs weighed before loading; weight variance vs estimate ≤±50 kg per ULD
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp-scale calibration drift (EASA Part-145 requirement: calibration every 12 months) causes systematic weight bias accumulating across all holds; discrepancies only surfaced at final W&B stage

l4_steps.name: Confirm ULD Weight Within Structural Limit
l4_steps.input: Actual ULD weight vs aircraft structural limit per bay (from Boeing aircraft performance data)
l4_steps.output: ULD cleared for loading or redistributed; updated hold allocation if rebalancing required
l4_steps.kpi: Zero structural limit exceedances reaching the aircraft; resolution time ≤8 min per overweight ULD
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft type changes (e.g. A320 substituted for A321) alter bay structural limits mid-process; SITA LoadManager aircraft config library updates lag fleet changes by 24–48 hours

l4_steps.name: Confirm Ground Equipment Positioning at Aircraft
l4_steps.input: Gate assignment from SITA AMS, loading start trigger from Load Controller
l4_steps.output: Baggage loaders / hi-loaders and belt loaders confirmed in position; loading authorised
l4_steps.kpi: GSE at aircraft ≤5 min after aircraft-on-blocks; zero loading delays attributable to GSE unavailability
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE pooling across multiple handlers at shared terminals creates resource contention; SITA AMS GSE tracking relies on manual check-in, not real-time GPS — actual vs reported positions diverge during peak banks

l4_steps.name: Load Cargo Holds per LIR Bay Assignment
l4_steps.input: LIR bay assignment, loaded ULDs/bulk bags at aircraft side
l4_steps.output: Items loaded into designated holds; barcode scan confirmation per piece
l4_steps.kpi: Loading compliance with LIR ≥99%; fwd/aft hold loaded within 20 min of start for narrowbody
l4_steps.pain_point: Handheld SITA LoadManager scan confirmation step is frequently skipped during high-tempo turns; missing scan events break baggage reconciliation and create BSM (Baggage Source Message) failures reported to IATA BRS

l4_steps.name: Load Special & Priority Items per NOTOC
l4_steps.input: Approved NOTOC, special cargo labels (live animals, wet ice, perishables, human remains)
l4_steps.output: Special cargo positioned per segregation rules and NOTOC; supervisor sign-off recorded
l4_steps.kpi: 100% NOTOC items loaded in approved positions; zero segregation violations on departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Live animal loading under IATA LAR requires temperature-zone compliance — cargo hold temperature monitoring (ACARS datalink) is not available on all aircraft types, creating regulatory exposure on LAR shipments

l4_steps.name: Verify Loading Sequence Matches LIR
l4_steps.input: Scan confirmations from step 3.2, LIR bay plan
l4_steps.output: Loading conformance report — approved to proceed or discrepancy flagged for correction
l4_steps.kpi: Loading conformance check completed before any hold door closed; discrepancy resolution ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Forward CG bias risk: ramp teams load forward holds first for efficiency; deviation from LIR sequence without re-run of W&B can produce an out-of-envelope CG that is only caught at step 4.3

l4_steps.name: Record Actual Loaded Weights per Hold
l4_steps.input: Scan-confirmed item list per hold bay from step 3.4
l4_steps.output: Actual hold-by-hold weight breakdown entered in LoadManager for final W&B run
l4_steps.kpi: All hold weights entered within 5 min of loading completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk-loaded items (oversized bags, strollers, wheelchairs) weighed individually at check-in but grouped in cargo manifests without piece-level tracking — cumulative weight error can exceed 100 kg on narrow-body aircraft

l4_steps.name: Compute Final ZFW, TOW & CG Position
l4_steps.system: SITA LoadManager + Boeing Aircraft Performance Tool (OPT)
l4_steps.input: Actual hold weights, confirmed fuel uplift, final pax count with no-shows applied
l4_steps.output: Final Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW), Take-Off Weight (TOW), Landing Weight (LW), and CG index value
l4_steps.kpi: Final W&B calculation completed ≤15 min before STD; TOW within ±0.5% of fuel plan
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing OPT structural limits database must match the exact aircraft tail number's modification status (SB-tracked changes alter limits); mismatches between OPT aircraft config and actual tail configuration require manual override with engineering sign-off

l4_steps.name: Confirm CG Within Certified Envelope
l4_steps.input: Final CG index, aircraft type CG envelope limits, trim setting
l4_steps.output: CG confirmed in-envelope and stabiliser trim setting issued to crew; or rebalance instruction issued
l4_steps.kpi: CG in-envelope on first calculation ≥95% of flights; rebalance time ≤15 min when required
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-of-no-return conflict: CG rebalance after door closure requires re-opening hold, adding 10–20 min to turnaround; pressure from OCC to depart on-time leads to borderline CG positions being accepted with minimal margin

l4_steps.name: Generate & Sign Final Loadsheet
l4_steps.input: Approved ZFW, TOW, CG, trim setting; final pax/bag count
l4_steps.output: Signed final loadsheet (paper or e-loadsheet) with load controller and captain signature blocks
l4_steps.kpi: Final loadsheet generated ≥15 min before STD; e-loadsheet adoption rate target ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory requirement for wet-ink captain signature on paper loadsheet persists at many airports due to incomplete e-loadsheet adoption under IATA Simplifying the Business (StB) programme; creates courier dependency and delays on remote stands

l4_steps.name: Transmit Final Loadsheet to Flight Deck via ACARS
l4_steps.input: Signed final loadsheet from SITA LoadManager
l4_steps.output: Loadsheet datalink message (LDM/CPM) received on flight deck EFB or ACARS printer
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS loadsheet delivery confirmed ≤12 min before STD; delivery failure rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS datalink congestion during peak departure banks (multiple aircraft departing simultaneously) causes transmission delays of 3–8 min; crews on ACARS-equipped EFBs (Jeppesen FliteDeck) may not receive message before paperwork cut-off

l4_steps.name: Obtain Crew Acknowledgment of Loadsheet
l4_steps.input: Loadsheet datalink message or paper copy delivered to flight deck
l4_steps.output: Crew acknowledgment uplinked via ACARS or paper signature returned; loadsheet accepted or queried
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgment received ≥10 min before STD; query resolution ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew queries about non-standard weights (e.g. cargo-only belly loads, heavy charters) require Load Controller to re-explain figures verbally — no structured digital query-and-response workflow exists in SITA LoadManager to track queries and responses for audit trail

l4_steps.name: Issue Last-Minute Change (LMC) if Required
l4_steps.input: Post-loadsheet change trigger (late pax, offload, security-removed bag)
l4_steps.output: LMC document transmitted to crew; updated ZFW/CG confirmed within limits
l4_steps.kpi: LMC issued and acknowledged ≤7 min before pushback; LMC rate <5% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: Security-driven offloads (unaccompanied baggage removal per IATA Resolution 753 BRS) can occur as late as T-5 min; cascading CG shift from forward-hold offload frequently triggers full W&B recalculation, compressing final clearance window to under 3 min

l4_steps.name: Close Cargo Doors & Issue Station Clearance
l4_steps.input: Crew acknowledgment confirmed, LMC resolved, all hold doors secured
l4_steps.output: Station departure clearance recorded in SITA AMS; ramp-clear signal issued to tug crew
l4_steps.kpi: Hold doors closed and ramp-clear signal issued ≥5 min before STD; on-time departure (D0) contribution ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent ground activities (refuelling, catering, water service) on the same aircraft require physical clearance coordination not tracked in SITA AMS — ramp supervisors rely on verbal radio confirmation, creating safety blind spots during rushed turns
